resolved_contract_gaps.title: Closed RG-07 action registry and atomic outcomes
resolved_contract_gaps.capability_boundary: The current v2 action registry has no closed discriminator/input contracts for refund request and status-only facts, receipt allocation and confirmation, imported confirmation, validation rejection, or reconciliation evidence merge.
resolved_contract_gaps.required_change: Register every planned action_type/operation_class pair listed in planned_action_registry. Accepted and no-change forms require their strict closed input; rejected forms require closed sparse attempted_input and forbid input. Retries retain the originating discriminator and never use a generic retry action. All forms require typed outcomes, complete deltas, stable IDs, and atomic zero-effect rejection.
resolved_contract_gaps.risk: An open input.kind or generic action/retry would make dispatch ambiguous, weaken sparse rejection closure, permit missing confirmations or over-cap partial acceptance, and duplicate formal or reconciliation effects.

resolved_contract_gaps.title: Refund relation and refund_relationship lifecycle
resolved_contract_gaps.capability_boundary: Current relation is false and refund_relationship has no closed domain payload.
resolved_contract_gaps.required_change: Register typed relation members plus a refund_relationship domain payload for inherited category, amounts, destination, distinct times, cumulative cap, and append-only history.
resolved_contract_gaps.risk: Untyped ownership could rewrite the original, lose accumulation, or blur relationship evidence and arrival evidence.

resolved_contract_gaps.title: Refund provenance payloads
resolved_contract_gaps.capability_boundary: Current source, candidate, confirmation, and evidence unions cannot represent RG-07 facts.
resolved_contract_gaps.required_change: Register closed merchant/manual/account-credit/mirror sources and evidence, refund candidate history, exact confirmations, hashes, times, and merge lineage.
resolved_contract_gaps.risk: Open provenance could promote the wrong evidence role, discard conflicts, or duplicate a receipt.
